title: Guarding the Heart of the Community

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Do not seek a treaty of friendship with them as long as you live. Do not despise an Edomite, for the Edomites are related to you. Do not despise an Egyptian, because you resided as foreigners in their country. The third generation of children born to them may enter the assembly of the Lord. - Deut 23:6-8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God gives careful, discerning instructions. Israel was not to pursue friendship with the nations that had actively sought their harm. Yet notice the balance, they were not to despise the Edomites, their relatives, nor the Egyptians, among whom they had once lived. In fact, the descendants of the Egyptians could eventually enter the assembly. God distinguishes between guarding against genuine spiritual danger and holding onto bitter grudges.

This is a wise and gracious balance. God did not want His people harbouring hatred, even toward former oppressors like Egypt. There was to be no despising, no nursing of resentment. At the same time, they were to be wise about influences that could corrupt them. God calls His people to discernment without bitterness.

We can learn much from this. It is possible to be wise and cautious about harmful influences while still refusing to despise or hate anyone. God calls us to guard our hearts without letting them grow bitter. Jesus went even further, teaching us to love our enemies and pray for those who persecute us (Matt 5:44). We hold two things together, discernment about what shapes us, and a heart free from hatred. God's grace even made room, over time, for former outsiders to be welcomed in. Is there someone you have been tempted to despise, whom God is calling you to release from your resentment?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there someone you have been tempted to despise?
2. How can you be discerning without becoming bitter?
3. What would it look like to release a grudge to God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me guard my heart wisely without holding on to bitterness. Teach me to love even those who have wronged me, as Christ loves me. Amen.
